1.text: FAMILY SHAMANISM. — Shamanism among the Chukchee, as has been

2.text: said before,¹ is in large measure affiliated with the family ceremonials. Each

3.text: family has one or more drums of its own, on which its members are bound

4.text: at specific periods to perform; that is, to accompany the beating of the drum

5.text: with the singing of various melodies. Almost always, on these occasions, one

6.text: member at least of the family tries to communicate with “spirits”. after the

7.text: manner of shamans. Such a one will usually, with violent shouting and con-

8.text: tinuous exercise on the drum, work himself up to the highest pitch possible,

9.text: and in this condition pretend that the “spirits” have entered his body. In

10.text: proof of this, he acts in exactly the same way as do the shamans, — jumping

11.text: about, twisting his body in the most violent contortions, and uttering gibbering

12.text: sounds and unintelligible words supposed to be the voice and the language

13.text: of the “spirits.” Oftentimes he essays soothsaying and foretelling the future,

14.text: though such attempts do not usually receive much attention. All this is done

17.text: The acts of real shamanism, on the contrary, are for the most part per-

18.text: formed in the sleeping-room, at night-time and in perfect darkness. They

19.text: are performed without preparation, on varied occasions, though usually the

20.text: days of the ceremonials are terminated by a performance of this kind carried

21.text: out during the night in the sleeping-room. The shamanistic acts, however,

22.text: are by no means restricted to the ceremonials, but accompany the activity of

23.text: the shaman proper in his own special calling. Nevertheless almost every

26.text: Besides this, every adult Chukchee will occasionally take his drum, espe-

27.text: cially in the winter, and beat it for a while under the warm shelter of the

28.text: sleeping-room, with the light or without it, singing his melodies to the rhythm

29.text: of the beats. This he does merely for his own pleasure. The transition from

30.text: such songs to shamanistic performances is quite imperceptible, and in this way

31.text: it is fair to say that every Chukchee may play the shaman in all branches of

32.text: the craft as far as his skill and inclination permit him to do so.

33.text: Family shamanism, being quite simple and primitive, probably ante-

34.text: dated the shamanism of individuals having special skill and vocation, and the

35.text: latter seems to have grown up based on the former. Family shamanism
